abstract: Running behavioral experiments is expensive, slow, and prone to design flaws, often detectable after collecting data. We introduce UnexpectedParrots to iteratively refine behavioral study designs before a researcher recruits costly human participants. UnexpectedParrots relies on reasoning traces in addition to responses from LLM participants to uncover diagnostic critiques of structural errors and missed opportunities in existing study designs. When evaluated against a human-pilot or a no-simulation design-only baseline, UnexpectedParrots adds most value, producing unique, high-quality critiques. In a moderated user study with 12 proficient researchers, we find UnexpectedParrots useful, time-saving, and thought-provoking. Critiques provided by UnexpectedParrots often converge on issues researchers identify only during independent human pilots or additional formative interviews, even when the fidelity of the simulated populations remains questionable. Our users deem UnexpectedParrots useful not only as a tool to conduct early pilot studies and identify errors but also as an ideation tool to expand one's research horizon.

ur.tldr: 提出UnexpectedParrots系统，在招募真人前借助LLM模拟参与者及其推理痕迹迭代优化行为实验设计。与人工预实验和纯设计基线相比，该系统产出独特且高质量的诊断性批评，能发现研究者通常在独立预实验或形成性访谈中才识别出的结构性问题。12名熟练研究人员用户研究表明其节省时间、启发思考、引发反思，可同时作为早期预实验工具与扩展研究视野的创意工具。

title: UnexpectedParrots: Iterating Behavioral Experiment Design with In-Silico Simulations
title_zh: UnexpectedParrots：利用计算机模拟迭代行为实验设计
